newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends sharply higher on spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends sharply higher on spec buying.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures rose sharply on Wednesday, ending at 1-1/2 week highs, on keen speculative buying amid lingering concerns about El Nino and the size of the upcoming Ivorian crop, dealers said.

"The specs started buying the market," said Refco analyst Ann Prendergast. "There's still some belief that El Nino will widen the deficit and that dry weather will have an effect on the Ivorian new crop."
September cocoa jumped $28 per tonne on the day, to $1,538, after ranging between $1,550 and $1,500. Second-month December closed $26 higher, at $1,585, while the back months also finished up $24.

The cocoa market fell at the opening, but came in short of its $10-$15 due. Dealers said light manufacturer interest toward the lows stemmed further losses and prompted a bout of local short covering.

Speculator joined in on the buying after September broke nearby chart resistance at $1,520 and touched off light buy-stops near $1,525, driving the spot contract toward the key $1,540 level, traders said.
Upward momentum accelerated after September broke $1,540 per tonne, touching off more buy-stops, traders said.
Continued concerns that a strong El Nino pattern could adversely impact cocoa crops -- particularly in Indonesia, Malaysia and Ecuador -- helped set a bullish tone.
Worries that recent dry weather in West Africa could effect the developing 1997/98 Ivorian main crop also underpinned sentiment.
"The crop is late and there's dry weather at the moment, so there's some uncertainty about survival," said one trader.

Traders said there were rumors private forecaster Hans Kilian put the 1997/98 Ivorian main crop at 880,000 to 900,000 tonnes, which was higher than his previous forecast, they said, but below some expectations of one million tonnes.
Reached in New Orleans, Kilian refused to comment.
Some traders said today's finish was encouraging and could lead to further buying on Thursday, while other traders expected the market to consolidate in the near-term.
Technically, traders said September faced resistance at today's high of $1,550, followed by a chart gap between $1,561 and $1,570. On the down side, support was seen at $1,535 and then $1,510.
Volume on tha day reached an estimated 9,786 lots.
